_note: Template — fill in every empty field before running an audit. run_queries.py refuses to run while any are blank. These values fill the {placeholders} in query_grid.json, so write each one the way it should read inside a buyer's question.
_brand: The brand name exactly as a buyer would type it, e.g. 'Hyperbound'.
_category: The product category as a buyer would phrase it in a question, lowercase, no trailing word like 'tools' (the queries add that), e.g. 'AI sales roleplay and training software'.
_category_short: A 2-4 word shorthand of the category for conversational queries, e.g. 'AI sales roleplay'.
_buyer_query_context: Who is asking and why, completing the sentence 'I'm ...', e.g. 'a sales leader evaluating tools to help SDRs practice cold calls'.
_competitors: Exactly 3 direct competitors a buyer would shortlist alongside the brand, most direct first. They fill {competitor_0}, {competitor_1}, {competitor_2} in the comparison queries.
_models: Which model each provider uses. Working defaults — leave them unless a model is retired or responses come back truncated (see README gotchas).
_max_tokens: Response cap per query. 700 is the tested default; the script adds headroom for Gemini thinking models automatically.
